title: quantization-debug-scratchpad-int8-fp8-bf16-maya-2026-03-04
content:
Summary:
- Working notes for NaN / quality regressions seen after quantizing 7B/13B models to INT8/FP8/BF16 variants. Mostly reproduces on our in-house 7B (gpt-like) model.

Context / quick timeline:
- 2026-02-18: initial INT8 conversion (per-tensor, symmetric) looked fine on toy prompts.
- 2026-02-22: first NaN report in staging: model emits <nan> logits after ~3 tokens for some prompts.
- 2026-02-24..26: tried per-channel scales, calibration with 128/512 samples, still intermittent NaNs and quality drop (weird repetitions).
- 2026-03-01: tried keeping LayerNorm/Bias in BF16, attention in INT8 -> fewer NaNs but still wrong outputs.
- 2026-03-03: reproduced locally and started bisecting which layers trigger NaN.

Commands / conversion steps I've tried (notes inline):
1) conversion (baseline):
   python tools/quantize.py --model ./models/7b-fp32 --out ./models/7b-int8 --method per-tensor --bits 8 --calib-samples 128
   -> log: "Conversion complete. max_scale=13.7, mean_scale=2.9"
   -> inference: sometimes NaN at step 3

2) per-channel quantization:
   python tools/quantize.py --model ./models/7b-fp32 --out ./models/7b-int8-ch --method per-channel --bits 8 --calib-samples 512
   -> log: "per-channel scales computed. warning: 0.6% channels scale>20"
   -> inference: fewer NaNs but occasional softmax blowups (very large logits -> inf -> nan)

3) keep norm params in bf16 (partial quant):
   python tools/quantize.py --model ./models/7b-fp32 --out ./models/7b-int8-partial --keep-params LayerNorm,Bias --bits 8
   -> inference: much improved stability; NaN frequency drops to ~1/200 prompts

4) FP8 experiment (experimental backend):
   python tools/quantize.py --model ./models/7b-fp32 --out ./models/7b-fp8 --method fp8-e4m3 --calib 256
   -> logs: "FP8 conversion OK, fallback kernels enabled"
   -> inference: still NaNs but different failure pattern (NaN appears later, often in attention score computation)

Repro snippet (run_inference output):
> prompt: "The capital of France is"
> token 0 logits: [ -1.2, 0.3, 0.9, ... ]
> token 1 logits: [ 0.5, 0.2, ... ]
> token 2 logits: [ nan, nan, nan, ... ]
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "run_inference.py", line 128, in step
    logits = model.step(tokens)
  File "/workspace/serving/runtime/ops/quant_matmul.cc", line 42, in quant_matmul
    throw runtime_error("NaN in output")
RuntimeError: NaN in output

Observations / hypotheses:
- LayerNorm seems sensitive: keeping LayerNorm weights in BF16 eliminates most NaNs. Prob: our quantization pipeline is applying scale/zero-point incorrectly to LayerNorm gamma/beta or to residual add before norm.
- Softmax overflow: very large logits -> exp overflow -> inf -> NaN. Could be mismatch in numeric range because scales are too large for some rows.
- Per-tensor scales fail on some heads/rows; per-channel helps but not perfect (we still see occasional huge scales).
- KV cache accumulation: if cached keys/values are stored in lower precision without proper accumulation (no FP32 accumulation) errors may amplify over tokens.
- Rotary or pos-emb mismatch: if rotary scaling or sin/cos factors are not quantized/handled consistently, can produce invalid values.
- Quantization of bias terms: biases cause shift; asymmetric vs symmetric quantization matters. We may be applying symmetric quant to biases which should stay FP32.
- Zero-point misapplication: using 0 zero-point assumption in asymmetric flow leads to offset errors in matmul accumulation.

Immediate tests to run (prioritized):
1) Minimal single-layer reproduction:
   - isolate one transformer block (layer i) and run FP32 vs INT8 matmul on same input, compare outputs and per-element differences
   - save intermediate (pre- and post- layernorm, attention scores) to disk for comparison

2) Disable quant for specific components (quick flags):
   --no-quant-layernorm, --no-quant-bias, --no-quant-pos
   Run for each layer and record whether NaN disappears; build a small map of "layers that trigger NaN"

3) Scale clamp experiments:
   - during conversion, clip scales to max_S (try 8, 12, 16) and add epsilon=1e-6 to division to avoid divide-by-zero

4) Calibration changes:
   - use percentile-based calibration (p99.999) instead of max to avoid outlier-dominated scales
   - try different calibration datasets (short prompts vs long dialogues)

5) Activation accumulation precision:
   - force accumulation in FP32 in quant kernels (if supported) and re-run inference to see if NaN frequency changes

6) Compare symmetric vs asymmetric quant for weights+bias separately

Additional logs I captured (snippets):
- converter warning: "channel 143 scale=72.4 > threshold 64; divided into two scales" (we don't actually split)
- runtime warn: "matmul_accum overflow near row 432"
- python-level: "RuntimeWarning: overflow encountered in exp" in softmax implementation

Notes from Ben (quick):
- "we saw a similar pattern last quarter; root cause was a bug in the reorder step for QKV when switching to per-channel scales — indices were being transposed incorrectly for some even/odd heads. Fixed by aligning reorder with scale axis."

Open questions / unknowns:
- Are we quantizing rotary/sinusoidal tables? If so, is there a mismatch in dtype when those are multiplied into attention?
- Do our fused kernels assume a particular layout (e.g. [head, d_head]) ordering that the converter sometimes swaps?
- Is there any hardware-specific behavior on A100 vs H100 for FP8 emulation that causes different rounding/inf behavior?

Next concrete steps (this week):
- Run single-layer reproducibility tests for layers 0, N//2, N-1 and collect intermediate tensors (Maya)
- Add a small debug build of quant_matmul that dumps scales, zero-points, and accumulators for the failing row (Ben)
- Try keeping layernorm and final output projection in BF16 and quantize rest (Lina)
- Schedule a quick pairing session to bisect head reordering (Thu 11am PT)

Useful commands / helpers (notes to self):
- dump tensors: python tools/dump_layer.py --model <path> --layer 10 --out dump/l10 --tokens "The capital of France is"
- run single layer debug: python tools/run_layer_debug.py --model <path> --layer 10 --quant-mode int8 --compare-fp32
- quick conversion with clamp: python tools/quantize.py --model ... --bits 8 --clamp-scale 12 --eps 1e-6

Acceptance criteria for a fix:
- No NaN for >10k randomized prompts (smoke test)
- Logit L2 difference < 1e-3 vs FP32 baseline on a suite of 200 calibration prompts (for non-critical tasks)
- No regression in ROUGE / BLEU on eval suite > 0.5% absolute drop

References / similar incidents:
- past incident: confluence:quantization-nan-incident (Jan 2026) — root cause there was reorder bug for qkv per-channel conversion
- upstream: github.com/xyz/quantlib issue #123 (softmax overflow with per-tensor scales)

TODO (short):
- [ ] run single-layer dumps for layers 0, mid, last
- [ ] implement percentile calibration in quantize-toolkit
- [ ] add guarding clamps in quant_matmul kernel for exp() inputs
- [ ] pair with Ben Thu 11am PT

Notes to self: keep logs for each experiment (date prefix). When a NaN reproduces, capture exact calibration file and seed. Don't trust "works sometimes".

-- Maya
